SNRIs, Atypical Antidepressants and MAOIs

venlafaxine, duloxetine · bupropion · mirtazapine · trazodone · monoamine oxidase inhibitorsWhich drug, which effect, and what does it rule out?

Practice
  1. 23-year-old woman with depression asks for an antidepressant binges and vomits several times a week; wants to quit smoking worried about weight gain on other drugs potassium 3.1 mEq/L · chloride 92 mEq/L → Bupropion → bupropion is contraindicated in bulimia and anorexia because it lowers the seizure threshold and purging disturbs electrolytes; SSRIs remain first-line antidepressants
  2. 41-year-old man with depression unresponsive to four antidepressant trials now on fluoxetine; his psychiatrist plans tranylcypromine no psychotic features, no suicidal ideation asks when the new drug can start BP 124/80 mm Hg · HR 72/min → Stop fluoxetine, wait 5 weeks, then start → fluoxetine has a long half-life, so 5 weeks must pass before an MAOI; 2 weeks is enough after other serotonergic drugs, and any overlap risks serotonin syndrome
  3. 48-year-old woman on phenelzine at a wine-and-cheese party sudden blurred vision and drenching sweat no new medicines; no tremor or clonus BP 228/124 mm Hg · HR 112/min · T 37.1 °C → Phentolamine → wine and aged cheese on an MAOI bring a tyramine hypertensive crisis, treated with phentolamine; cyproheptadine is for serotonin syndrome, and physostigmine for anticholinergic toxicity with hot, dry skin
  4. 56-year-old man on phenelzine given meperidine after knee surgery 3 hours later agitated, sweating and shivering hyperreflexia; clonus at both ankles T 39.4 °C · BP 168/96 mm Hg · HR 124/min → Serotonin syndrome → meperidine is contraindicated with an MAOI because the pair causes serotonin syndrome, typically fever, autonomic instability, hyperreflexia and clonus; the tyramine crisis follows aged food or a sympathomimetic, and anticholinergic toxicity leaves the skin dry
  5. 38-year-old man with a painful erection lasting 6 hours began a sedating antidepressant at bedtime 2 weeks ago no sickle cell disease; no injected erectile drugs BP 118/76 mm Hg · HR 88/min → Trazodone → trazodone blocks alpha-1 receptors and can cause priapism; bupropion causes insomnia and no sexual dysfunction, and mirtazapine sedates and raises appetite without sexual dysfunction
  6. 78-year-old woman with depression, poor sleep and weight loss starts mirtazapine at bedtime no seizures, eating disorder or heart disease weight 48 kg, down 4 kg · BP 128/74 mm Hg → Increased appetite and weight gain → mirtazapine blocks histamine H1 receptors, so it sedates and raises appetite and weight, welcome here; insomnia belongs to bupropion, and mirtazapine causes no sexual dysfunction
  7. 52-year-old man with generalized anxiety disorder at a follow-up visit venlafaxine dose doubled 2 months ago; trazodone at bedtime no new drugs, salt or alcohol change BP 154/98 mm Hg, was 126/80 · HR 92/min → Venlafaxine → venlafaxine raises blood pressure in a dose-dependent way and is typically avoided in hypertension; trazodone blocks alpha-1 receptors and lowers blood pressure on standing
  8. 34-year-old woman stopped venlafaxine abruptly 2 days ago felt well for a year; ran out of pills now dizzy, nauseated, irritable, achy as if with flu T 37.0 °C · no seizures → Restart venlafaxine, then taper slowly → abrupt stops of venlafaxine, a short half-life drug, bring discontinuation symptoms within days, flu-like among them; restarting and tapering slowly treats them

Transferable rule

Name the drug, then its rule: an MAOI never meets tyramine or another serotonergic drug (2 weeks between an MAOI and a serotonergic drug; 5 weeks after fluoxetine); bupropion stays away from seizures and purging; trazodone can cause priapism, mirtazapine weight gain, venlafaxine hypertension.
